artifacts.notes: Audit metadata for the former normalized payload: one header line and 121 data lines, one physical line per printed sense line, with no embedded tabs or newlines; sha256 and byte_size above identify the exact removed bytes. The payload is not tracked, indexable, or an assembled-liturgical-text source. This ecumenical text is not the Roman Missal's approved English, and the copyright grant is not liturgical approval. Retaining the hash and transformation/source evidence does not authorize reconstructing or serving the wording from another corpus.
artifacts.rights_basis: The rightsholder grants free use in terms, on its own permissions page and again in its Guidelines for Reproducing ELLC Texts: "The texts in Praying Together may be used freely and without the need for prior permission. The liturgical text(s) should be properly acknowledged." Both statements were read from bytes fetched and hashed by this project on 2026-07-31 and are registered as the sibling permissions-page and reproduction-guidelines artifacts. The grant is to the liturgical texts only; the Consultation's introduction and its notes on each text are expressly excluded. The acknowledgement the grant requires is: English translations of the Kyrie eleison, Gloria in excelsis, the Nicene Creed, the Apostles' Creed, the Sursum corda, the Sanctus and Benedictus, the Agnus Dei, the Lord's Prayer and the Gloria Patri, (c) 1998, English Language Liturgical Consultation (ELLC), and used by permission. www.englishtexts.org. The grant also expects the printed sense lines to be kept. The former tracked TSV did preserve one physical row per sense line, but its raw public-Git/download surface did not carry the required acknowledgement at the point of use and the repository's assembled Day/Missal surfaces cannot treat this ecumenical text as approved Roman-Rite English. The payload is therefore removed from the current tree and this record is text-free, restricted source evidence. A future explicitly labelled non-recitation source-study view would require a separate surface decision proving that the exact acknowledgement and sense lines travel with every served copy.

edition.publication: English Language Liturgical Consultation, 1998. The texts and the Consultation's commentary on each are published on the Consultation's own site at https://www.englishtexts.org/, one page per text.
edition.title: Praying Together, the 1998 revision of the ELLC common liturgical texts

work.author: English Language Liturgical Consultation (ELLC), successor to the International Consultation on English Texts (ICET)
work.description: The ecumenical English translations of the liturgical texts the Western churches hold in common: the Lord's Prayer, Kyrie eleison, Gloria in excelsis, the Nicene and Apostles' Creeds, the Sursum corda, the Sanctus and Benedictus, the Agnus Dei, the Gloria Patri, the Te Deum, and the three gospel canticles. ELLC is an ecumenical consultation of English-speaking liturgical bodies and is not an organ of any one church. These translations are therefore NOT the approved liturgical English of the Roman Rite: the Roman Missal's English is the International Commission on English in the Liturgy's, a different body with a different text, and the two must never be conflated. Where the two are compared the difference is visible at once - this work reads 'And also with you' where the 2011 Roman Missal reads 'And with your spirit', and 'We believe in one God' where it reads 'I believe in one God'.
work.title: Praying Together
